settings.emulator.intro: BreadCraft can find VICE automatically — or pick the folder where VICE lives and BreadCraft locates the right executable ({exe}) inside it. This lets BreadCraft test a built program directly in the emulator until the embedded emulator is available.

about.title: About BreadCraft
about.tagline: A tool that turns your idea into a real C64 game.
about.license: BreadCraft itself is under the MIT license.
about.cc65Body: cc65 translates your programs into real C64 machine code. It ships inside BreadCraft and is under the zlib license.
about.viceBody: VICE is the C64 your programs run on. It is free software under the GPL — so we don't bundle it; we fetch it from the official source on first run.
onboarding.title: Ready for your C64
onboarding.foundIntro: BreadCraft found a C64 emulator (VICE) on your machine:
onboarding.foundWhy: With it, you'll see your programs run on a real C64 right away.
onboarding.missingIntro: To watch your programs run, BreadCraft needs VICE — a C64 to see them on. None is set up on your machine yet.
onboarding.downloadHint: Opens the VICE page in your browser. Then choose the folder you unpacked it to below.
onboarding.licenseNote: VICE is free software (GPL) and is fetched from the official VICE page.
onboarding.link: I already have it — choose folder
onboarding.linkHint: Point at the folder where VICE lives. BreadCraft finds the executable itself.
onboarding.laterHint: No must: writing and building programs works without it. You only need VICE to run them.
onboarding.dlPatience: This takes a moment — VICE is about 47 MB.
onboarding.dlErrorBody: Maybe the connection dropped for a moment. You can try again, get VICE by hand, or choose a folder you already have.
onboarding.dlErrorChecksum: The downloaded file was corrupted (its checksum didn't match). It was discarded for safety — nothing was installed. Best to try again.
onboarding.openPageHint: Download in your browser, then choose the folder here.

palette.hiresNote: In hi-res mode each character has only two colours — the background here, plus one free colour per cell. The shared multicolor colours don't exist here, so the editor hides them.

tilemap.clearConfirm: Empty the whole map? This cannot be undone.

tilemap.noCharset: Paint some characters in the PETSCII editor first — those are the tiles here.
tilemap.bandWarn: above {max} rows today's technique no longer scrolls smoothly
tilemap.bandTitle: Drag me. Between the two lines the world scrolls; above and below the picture stands still — that is where your score lives. Up to {max} tile rows BreadCraft's current scrolling technique runs like butter; beyond that the picture gets rough. The C64 itself can do more with double buffering — that upgrade is on the roadmap. In your program you say the same thing with PlayField.
tilemap.levelSizeTitle: How long your level is. One screen of level costs the C64 about 400 bytes — this one costs {bytes}. Paint into the hatched strip on the right and the level grows by a screen.
tilemap.levelSizePerCell: This level costs {bytes} bytes — twice as much per column as usual. The reason: you painted tile(s) {tiles} in more than one colour. As long as every tile keeps ONE colour, a small colour table says it all; the moment a tile carries two, the colour has to travel with every single cell. It isn't forbidden — the C64 can do it, it just costs.
tilemap.fitViewTitle: Bring the whole map into the window

image.penHint: Left paints the primary colour, right the secondary (right-click a swatch to set it). The gradient dithers between them: drag a line to set direction + length. The select tool drags a frame that tools act inside (Ctrl+D clears it). Wheel zooms to the cursor, middle-drag pans.

image.mode.freeHint: Paint with all 16 colours, no per-cell limit — like DPaint. The readout still shows where you exceed the C64 budget.
image.mode.c64Hint: Keep every 8×8 cell C64-legal (background + 3 colours). A fourth colour snaps to the nearest one the cell can afford.
image.c64preview.hint: Show the canvas as the real C64 image — each cell forced to background + 3 colours. See lost pixels here, not as a surprise in the build.
